ratings_why.fun: Over a 7 because order is the puzzle on every board: Ilse before or after the King, the Bean-Counter at the end of the line, Fips throwing news across a gap, and the Thirty-Two copying whatever texts you own, so the same cards make a different machine each game.
ratings_why.distinct: A spill rule on the touching zigzag, carried by any tribe and aimable at the enemy, plays unlike today's tribes, though a threshold counter that pays out is familiar from other games.

verdict_why: The core is ready; one rule about Gossip above the threshold needs writing down, because Hearth Huddle pays on exactly that count.

points.text: Blurt says a unit that already Blurted holds extra Gossip for later, but not whether it can hold 3 or more, or whether it Blurts when the chain ends. Hearth Huddle pays per Gossip held, so this decides whether a middle unit can bank 4 to 6 pips a turn; write the rule (for example, cap at 2 held, or Blurt in the next chain).

Ratskeller Landlady's "three times a turn" doesn't say whether it counts Blurts or uses of the text, which changes the gold under the Town-Hall Bellringer, Mill-Chimney Echo or a Thirty-Two copy. Say which.
The Bad Omen against a Piper player makes every enemy Blurt into an extra enemy attack. That mirror twist is a delight worth keeping, and a line in the builds would help players spot it.

Speaker Brotkrume has no Blurt text, so Echo, Bellringer and the Thirty-Two can't touch it. A golden or Tier 6 hook that copies its spread shape (next to, not touching) would give the hub its own combo line.
Cold-Shed Tangle's Strays could start with 1 or 2 Gossip, so a Stray that fills a gap mid-fight re-lights the wire instead of only reconnecting it.

standouts.why: A threshold-1 hub that spreads sideways too turns a line into a star; where you put him reshapes the whole wire.
Points the mechanic at the enemy board, so their own layout and gaps become your weapon or their defence.
Copies every Blurt text you own, so each new Rat and each outsider changes what it does.

weakest.why: A spark on play and +1/+1; it does its one job and never interacts again.
A generic Discover reward for chain length; it adds no decision to how you wire the board.
1/1 Strays are filler unless the chain needs a gap filled; little reason to build around it.

flags.note: Pays per Gossip held, and how much Gossip a unit can hold after a chain is not settled (point p1).
A fully loaded board can make seven attacks at Start of Combat before the enemy acts; the designer lists this too.
Two Gossip on every enemy plus one hit can damage the whole enemy run at once; gaps are the only counterplay.
Under the Rat King a 5-Blurt chain is guaranteed every turn, so this becomes a free Discover each turn.
The three-a-turn cap is unclear under multipliers (point p2).
